messages:
tom: heads-up — CI from yesterday shows a ~18% token-step slowdown for the fp8 kernels when we enable the new calibration pipeline. Perf trace points to kernel fallback on short-seq batches and extra memcpy around kv cache warmup :eyes:
leila: can you paste the flamegraph / perf output? small regressions like that often hide batching heuristics issues
Tom: paste below (trimmed):
```
Flamegraph top: 1) fp8_gemm_kernel (hot) 2) fallback_to_int8_path 3) kv_cache_prefetch 4) cudaMemcpyAsync
Hotspots by time: fp8_gemm_kernel 42%, fallback 20%, kv ops 18%, overhead 10%
```
leila: hmm fallback path showing up is weird — suggests quant params from calibration are mapping layers to kernels that our runtime marks as incompatible for short seqlen, so runtime switches to a safer, slower path
miguel: did the calib set change? I remember we recently added a batch of instruction-following dialogs with lots of short prompts
Tom: yes — we switched from a mixed-length corpus (0.5-512) to a heavy short-tail (0-64) to try to better capture prefix patterns. That was the main change in the per-channel calib run.
sara: quick note: per-channel usually improves accuracy but can increase kernel variance and cause more kernel-specialization. With many short examples we might be biasing scale/zero-point estimators causing kernel dispatch to pick different kernels
leila: actionable repro: run the quant bench with --batch-sizes 1,4,8 and seq buckets [8,32,128] and enable --trace-kernel-dispatch to see which kernels are used per-layer
Tom: ran that, output: layer 3/12 uses fp8_fast for seq>=128, fp8_fallback for seq<128, but with per-channel calib fp8_fast selection threshold bumped to >256 for some layers — so with short seqs we hit fallback often
miguel: sounds like calibration produced per-channel scales that violate our kernel constraints (e.g. too many small scales -> dequant saturation risk), so runtime conservatively avoids fast kernel. We have two axes: adjust calibration to clip outliers, or relax kernel constraints at risk of correctness
sara: for outliers, I propose percentile trimming: drop top 0.2% of absolute activation values per-channel before computing scale, and additionally compute both per-tensor and per-channel scales and choose the one with lower dynamic range ratio. Keeps benefits but reduces variance
leila: +1. Another idea: bucketized calibration — compute scales separately per-length bucket (short/med/long) and emit a single tuned per-layer choice plus a heuristic to prefer per-tensor for layers that flip between kernels across buckets
Tom: bucketized sounds promising but increases cost and complexity for on-device quant tables and rollout. For Hosted we can store multiple calibs and route traffic, but for private/offline deploys it's messier
miguel: regarding runtime fallback: we can also improve kernel selection logic to consider batch-size and kv cache state. Right now selection is a static comparison on scale values; it should be dynamic: if kv_cache warmup detected (first token calls) favor low-latency kernel even if scale borderline
sara: that's risky — favoring low-latency kernel might reduce numeric fidelity on rare cases. But we can add an A/B gating: if we switch kernel for warmup tokens, compute sample diff on a few tokens and fallback if error > epsilon
Tom: good middle ground. Also: we should add calibration dataset guidance — include representative warmup tails (e.g., 1-8 token continuations) plus some long-form contexts. Current short-only set biased kernel decisions
leila: I'll open a small repro script and a dataset sampler that enforces: 60% short (1-64), 30% mid (65-256), 10% long (257+), plus synthetic "warmup" sequences that repeat typical prompt prefix patterns. Putting seed and sampling code below: 
```
# sampler pseudocode
buckets = [(1,64,0.6),(65,256,0.3),(257,1024,0.1)]
for i in range(N):
  b = weighted_choice(buckets)
  seq = sample_from_corpus(length=random_in(b))
  if random()<0.05: seq = append_warmup(seq)
  emit(seq)
```
miguel: what about outlier-handling code? I'd add two passes: first compute per-channel percentiles, then clip at p99.8 and re-evaluate scales, emit both per-tensor and per-channel candidates with a metric (ratio of max/min activation)
Tom: let's try pipeline: 1) bucketized sampling; 2) p99.8 trimming per-channel; 3) compute both per-tensor and per-channel; 4) run kernel-dispatch sim to see if per-channel would cause fallback on typical batch/seq distributions; 5) if fallback frequency > 5% pick per-tensor or trimmed per-channel 6) log decisions to telemetry
sara: add telemetry: per-layer fallback frequency, avg token latency delta, and small accuracy check on a holdout eval set (EM/ROUGE or classification acc as applicable)
perf-bot: perf-regression-checker: New run triggered for branch quant-calib-bucketized by @leila. Baseline: commit 2025-11-02. Noted metrics will be collected and reported to #eng-ml after run completes.
leila: I'll prep the PR with sampler + clipping + kernel-sim. Can someone own adding the dynamic kernel-selection-for-warmup prototype? miguel?
miguel: happy to. I'll try a conservative A/B where we switch kernel only for first 4 tokens and compute per-request delta; if mean delta < 1e-3 then keep policy
Tom: perfect. After we have telemetry we can decide whether to default per-channel or fall back to trimmed per-channel/per-tensor hybrid. Thank you all :thumbsup:
sara: once we have results, let's also test with dedicated (high-batch) and hosted (small-batch, streaming) workloads — behavior differs widely.
Tom: agreed. Will post the perf logs and flamegraphs in this thread when CI finishes.
